Ram Chand's staff of devotion is such that it has killed the disease of ego. For example: when Hari, taking the form of Narsingh, killed Harnakhas, protected the devotee Prahlad and gave him the throne, after some time, through bad company, the devotee Prahlad was overtaken by the pride of rule. To avenge his father he made ready his whole army to fight Parmeshar. Then Hari took the form of an old Brahmin, came to Prahlad and said: "Against whom have you made ready your army?" Prahlad said: "Parmeshar killed my father; now I will kill him and take revenge." Then the Brahmin said: "You have done well. He killed my father and grandfather too; I also wanted revenge, and with your help I will take it. But where does he live?" Prahlad said: "I don't know where he lives either; wherever we find him, we'll kill him." As they spoke, the Brahmin's staff fell, and the Brahmin said: "Hand me this staff; I am old and can't lift it." Then Prahlad put great strength into lifting the staff, but it would not rise. Then the Brahmin said: "Is it on the strength of this that you want to fight Parmeshar?"
